title: Make the required gate fast for low-risk PRs and stop reporting a slow gate as red
body:
Outcome: a small, low-risk PR reaches a green required `krn/gate` in minutes, not tens of minutes, and deliver never reports a slow gate as a failure.
Operator mandate 2026-11-05 (verbatim): "strukturalnie musisz wszystko ogarnąć ten kod ma być perfekcyjny szefie" — granted after the lead proposed a diff-scoped gate for low-risk changes, which amends ADR 0014 D30 (full Product `krn/gate` required on every HEAD); record the amendment in the ADR in the same PR.
Facts:
- Main `krn/gate` took 12-13 min on the last 6 merges; PR #232 (3-line fix, t-vrbgwbk) ran 40+ min at host load 25 on 16 cores.
- Rootless containerd.service had CPUWeight=20; raised to 400 on 2026-11-05 (~/AGENTS.network.md). Measure gate time after the change before scoping.
- deliver exited 74 "ci: bounded wait timed out" while the gate was still in_progress: the same code as a red gate. A timeout must be a distinct, resumable outcome (or wait to the gate's own deadline).
Steps: (1) profile gate stages from Jenkins (which stage takes the 12 min); (2) fix the deliver timeout exit; (3) propose and implement the tiered gate (risk tier from `krn review --risk-tier`: low = affected tests + rules + preflight, full suite on main after merge) with the D30 amendment.
Proof: an observer for the deliver timeout outcome; a gate-duration measurement before/after on the same PR shape.

Reference (operator, 2026-11-05: pingdotgg/t3code release.yml screenshot + Theo/Astrid posts): wall clock comes from parallelism and skipped work, not fast tests. (a) cheap preflight 31 s and quality checks 49 s gate first, fail fast; (b) server tests sharded into an 8-job matrix, ~2 min each; (c) content-addressed skips: 'Check if the Rust blob is cached' builds only on a new input hash; the cache lives in R2 instead of GitHub cache to avoid evictions; (d) pnpm store cached (Astrid: their pnpm install alone took longer than Theo's build). For KRN: shard the gate suite across parallel containers by measured file duration; cache test results keyed by the hash of each test file's import closure + toolchain, skip unchanged; persist the pnpm store and node_modules by lockfile hash; order stages cheap-first. Measure each step separately (one change at a time).
